mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine replacement typically costs between £2,200 and £5,000 for a reconditioned unit, depending on engine code, condition, and supplier. Used EA189 units start from around £900, while EA288 reconditioned units range from £2,800 to £4,500. Supply and fit adds approximately £520-£715 in labour for an independent specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF failure in a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of DPF failure in a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI include a glowing DPF warning light on the dashboard, reduced engine performance, increased fuel consumption, and the car entering limp mode. You may also notice a strong smell of diesel or burning from the exhaust.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether it's worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI depends on the car's value and condition. For Mk2 Tiguan 2.0 TDI values above £8,000, a reconditioned engine with a 12-month warranty usually makes financial sense. For older Mk1 Tiguan 2.0 TDI cars worth under £4,000, a used engine or even scrapping the car may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine replacement typically takes 1-3 days for a specialist workshop, depending on whether the car is 2WD or 4Motion and whether it has a DSG gearbox. 4Motion all-wheel-drive models require additional labour for driveshaft and Haldex system disconnection. Most supply-and-fit bookings can be completed within a week of ordering.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Tiguan 2.0 TDI 150 and the 2.0 TDI 197?

acceptedAnswer.text: The difference is engine code and turbo specification. The Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI 150 (DFGA, DTSA) produces 148-150hp and is the UK's most common 2.0 TDI variant. The 2.0 TDI 197 (DTUA, sometimes badged as 200ps) produces 197hp and is typically found in higher-spec SEL and R-Line trims, often with 4Motion and DSG as standard.

mainEntity.name: Where is the engine code on a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine code is found in two places: on a sticker in the spare wheel well or the inside cover of the service book, and stamped on the engine block near the oil filter housing or on the cylinder head. The code is also listed on the vehicle's V5C registration document.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI arrived with the first-generation Tiguan in 2007 and has remained the UK's best-selling Tiguan engine, accounting for approximately 70% of sales. Over three generations - Typ 5N (2007-2016), Typ AD/BW (2016-2024), and the third generation (2024-present) - the 2.0 TDI has evolved through the EA189, EA288, and latest EA288 evo architectures, with power outputs ranging from 109hp to 236hp.

milestones.description: EA189 2.0 TDI (BKD, AZV) arrives with first-generation Tiguan, 138-168hp
2012 - CBAB, CBBB, CFFB, CFFD, CFGB codes introduced across facelift cycles
Second-generation Tiguan (Typ AD/BW) introduces EA288 2.0 TDI with CRBC, CRLB, DFGA, delivering 148-197hp
2.0 BiTDI 236hp joins range, available only in SEL and R-Line trims
DFG, DTE codes added; Allspace 7-seat variant shares all 2.0 TDI codes
Third-generation Tiguan introduces latest EA288 evo codes: DTRC (120hp), DTSA/DTSB/DXPA (148hp), DXNB (190hp), DTUA (197hp)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI is one of the UK's most popular diesel engines - but it's not without its weaknesses. EA189 units (2007-2015) are prone to DPF, EGR, and injector issues exacerbated by the Dieselgate software update, while EA288 units (2016 onwards) suffer AdBlue system faults and DPF sensitivity on short urban journeys. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Blockage & EGR Valve Carbonisation - "Why the Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI Suffers Emissions System Failures"
problems.rootCause: Urban driving prevents passive DPF regeneration; soot builds up and blocks the filter. The EGR valve recirculates exhaust gases and becomes clogged with carbon, especially in UK stop-start traffic.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical or off-car DPF clean; EGR valve removal and carbon blast
repairOptions.longevity: Buy time on a car you plan to sell; may recur within 20,000 miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New DPF and EGR valve fitted; software reset
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix; viable for cars worth over £4,000

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When combined with other failures (injectors, turbo); economically sensible for cars worth £5,000+

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical used Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI ranges from approximately £4,500 for an early Mk1 example to over £30,000 for a recent low-mileage Mk2. For Mk1 Tiguan 2.0 TDI values under £5,000, repair or a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For Mk2 values £8,000-£15,000, reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For vehicles £15,000+, replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If you're facing DPF and EGR failure on an older EA189 Tiguan worth under £4,000, a used engine may be the most cost-effective route. If you're keeping a Mk2 EA288 Tiguan for 2+ years and the car is worth £8,000+, the warranty and reliability of a reconditioned engine with upgraded components make financial sense. If the car is worth under £4,000 and requires a full engine replacement, honestly evaluate scrap value first.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EA189/EA288 Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue System Failure - "Why the Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI (EA288) AdBlue System Fails"
problems.rootCause: AdBlue pumps, NOx sensors, and heaters fail; crystallisation blocks injectors. Can trigger warning lights, non-start issues, and MOT failures if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan; software reset if no hardware failure
repairOptions.longevity: Intermittent faults; may not resolve hardware issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed AdBlue injector or pump; system flush
Supply & fit, includes AdBlue system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When combined with DPF or other failures; only for higher-value Tiguan 2.0 TDI examples

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - AdBlue system repairs can exceed £1,000 on an EA288 Tiguan. For vehicles under £5,000, weigh repair cost against value carefully.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue system failure is often a single-component issue - start with diagnostics before assuming full engine replacement is necessary. If the pump or injector has failed, specialist replacement at £400-£800 is typically better value than condemning the whole engine. However, if AdBlue failure accompanies DPF blockage, injector wear, or turbo issues on a high-mileage EA288 unit, a reconditioned engine becomes the more sensible long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EA288 Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Wear & Injector Failure - "Why the Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI Timing Belt and Injectors Need Attention"
problems.rootCause: Timing belt requires replacement at manufacturer intervals (typically 5 years / 80,000-100,000 miles). If it snaps, valves bend and engine destruction follows. Injector failure (coking on EA189, electrical faults on EA288) causes misfires, black smoke, and rough running.

repairOptions.longevity: Preventative maintenance - do at 80,000 miles or 5 years

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or reconditioned injectors; coding required
repairOptions.longevity: Viable for high-mileage units; good value if injectors are sole issue
When belt has snapped or injector failure has caused cylinder damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same value framework applies - preventative belt replacement is almost always cheaper than engine replacement.
problems.recommendation: This is the one failure where prevention is genuinely cheaper than cure. If you own a Volkswagen Tiguan 2.0 TDI approaching 80,000 miles and the belt hasn't been changed, book the specialist belt replacement immediately at £400-£700. If the belt has already snapped, the cost of a full engine rebuild or replacement is unavoidable - and for an older Mk1 Tiguan under £4,000, scrap value may be the honest answer.
